episodes.title: A 158-Year Shadow Over Millions of Citizens.

blocks.text:
In 1860, the British colonial administration enacted Section 377 of the Indian Penal Code, penalizing "unnatural offences" with up to life imprisonment.

For over a century and a half, this Victorian morality provision subjected millions of LGBTQ+ citizens to criminal prosecution, blackmail, and systemic denial of dignity.

FACTUAL MATRIX (Statement of Facts): In 1860, the British colonial administration enacted Section 377 of the Indian Penal Code, penalizing "unnatural offences" with up to life imprisonment.

For over a century and a half, this Victorian morality provision subjected millions of LGBTQ+ citizens to criminal prosecution, blackmail, and systemic denial of dignity. The legal controversy originated from whether the act committed fell within the statutory exceptions.

episodes.title: From Delhi High Court (Naz Foundation) to Suresh Koushal.

blocks.text:
In 2009, the Delhi High Court in **Naz Foundation** decriminalized homosexuality.

However, in 2013, the Supreme Court in **Suresh Kumar Koushal** overturned the ruling, calling the LGBTQ+ community a "miniscule fraction".

When the 9-judge bench in **Puttaswamy (2017)** affirmed privacy as a fundamental right, the stage was set for the final battle.

episodes.title: 6 September 2018: "History Owes an Apology".

blocks.text:
On 6 September 2018, all 5 judges delivered separate but unanimous opinions striking down Section 377 IPC insofar as it applied to consenting adults.

Justice Indu Malhotra wrote the famous words: **"History owes an apology to the members of this community and their families for the delay in providing redressal."**

CJI Dipak Misra declared: **"I am what I am, so take me as I am."**

episodes.title: The Doctrine of constitutional morality.

blocks.text:
The Navtej Johar ruling established that Indian courts exist to protect the counter-majoritarian rights of minorities.

Popular majoritarian sentiments cannot justify the state intruding into the private lives, bedrooms, and identities of sovereign citizens.

This judgment stands alongside Kesavananda Bharati as a masterwork of Indian constitutional freedom.

flashcards.q: Which court decided Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India and in what year?
flashcards.a: Supreme Court of India in the year 2018.

flashcards.q: What was the primary legal issue addressed in this case?
What is the core Ratio Decidendi of the judgment?
flashcards.a: A unanimous 5-judge Constitution Bench held that Section 377 IPC is unconstitutional insofar as it criminalizes consensual adult intimacy in private. The court upheld Section 377 only for non-consensual acts and bestiality.

flashcards.q: What is the primary citation for this ruling?
flashcards.a: Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India, (2018) 10 SCC 1, AIR 2018 SC 4321

flashcards.q: What is the current legal status of this precedent?
flashcards.a: Section 377 IPC read down to decriminalize consensual same-sex relations between adults.

affectsYou.heading: कानूनी निष्कर्ष
points: अदालत का फैसला निचली अदालतों के लिए बाध्यकारी है।

timeline.event: 5-judge Constitution Bench unanimously declares Section 377 unconstitutional for consenting adults.
BNS replaces IPC completely without re-enacting any provision criminalizing consensual adult sodomy.

subsequentHistory.note: Affirmed and applied in subsequent landmark jurisprudence.
